9301144.story:
Property owners in County Limerick are being urged to review their security measures following a series of recent break-ins targeting garden sheds across the county.

Authorities at Henry Street Garda Station have issued a public warning in the wake of the offences. https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53149.summary: Local secondary schools have expressed solidarity with Glenstal Abbey after the shock announcement that the historic boarding school will close by August 2028. Limerick secondary schools have spoken out in support of Glenstal Abbey following the shock announcement on October 23 that the school plans to close by August 2028.

Glenstal Abbey announced it would wind down operations no later than August 2028 after 94 years of providing secondary education to boys aged 12 to 18 since 1932. Leased for a trial period, the GHS Drive 1800 was used to cut and collect vegetation from grasslands and pollinator-friendly meadows within the Limerick Decarbonisation Zone and surrounding areas. Unlike traditional mowing methods, the machine cuts and removes vegetation in a single operation. This removal process is recognized as a best-practice technique that creates conditions for native wildflowers and pollinators to thrive.

The pilot program delivered several environmental and operational benefits, including reduced fuel consumption, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and less noise compared to conventional management methods. According to research, well-managed wildflower meadows encourage deeper root systems and increased soil carbon storage, transforming grasslands into valuable carbon sinks.

Following the success of the trial, Limerick City and County Council intends to explore purchasing a similar machine to support its long-term approach to sustainable grassland management and climate action, aligning with the Limerick Biodiversity Action Plan, the Climate Action Plan, and the All-Ireland Pollinator Plan.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.localAngle: The trial directly impacts local green spaces and decarbonisation efforts within Limerick City and County Council's jurisdiction.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362473.originalTitle: Zero gravity machine hitting heights in biodiversity

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.headline: Councillors Clash Over Plan to Transfer Six Abbeyfeale Properties to Limerick Twenty Thirty
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.summary: Local representatives have raised serious concerns after Mayor John Moran proposed handing over six council-owned properties in Abbeyfeale to project development company Limerick Twenty Thirty for a cost-recovery rental model.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.story:
Elected members in the Newcastle West district have warned the local authority that it risks "creating a monster" following proposals to dispose of six Council-owned properties in Abbeyfeale to Limerick Twenty Thirty Strategic Development DAC. The plan, tied to Mayor John Moran’s mayoral programme, aims to use the properties to provide a cost-recovery rental model for working households and key workers in the West Limerick town.

The properties involved include sites at Convent Road, 6 and 7 Colbert Terrace, 8 Old Church Street, and units 1 and 2 at the Bridge Inn, comprising a mix of one, two, three, and four-bed units. According to the Council, the intervention is designed to diversify the local housing offer, strengthen local spending power, and support long-term economic sustainability.

However, Fianna Fáil councillor Michael Collins strongly objected to the move during October’s district meeting, arguing that Limerick Twenty Thirty should focus on commercial developments rather than private housing matters. Cllr Collins called for an immediate workshop for all elected members and criticized a private meeting held between the Mayor and district Cathaoirleach Cllr Liam Galvin regarding the properties.

Cllr Galvin defended his involvement, explaining that the houses had been lying idle for two years and are now finished to a "Grade A standard" ready for mid-November. While noting he had initial reservations about the Mayor's proposed scheme, Cllr Galvin stated he is willing to give the initiative a chance to address community concerns over the vacant stock.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.localAngle: The dispute highlights ongoing debates among Limerick councillors over the division of commercial and private housing remits in county towns like Abbeyfeale.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362470.originalTitle: Proposed disposal of Abbeyfeale properties to Limerick Twenty Thirty raises serious questions

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.headline: Limerick Property Prices Rise by €10,000 to Reach Median Asking Price of €290,000
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.summary: Property prices across Limerick have increased by €10,000 over the past year, bringing the median asking price to €290,000 according to the latest Q3 report. While overall prices remained flat over the quarter, availability grew with 444 properties listed for sale.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.story:
Property prices in Limerick have climbed by €10,000 over the past year, bringing the median asking price for a home in the county to €290,000, according to the latest MyHome Property Price Report for the third quarter of 2026. While overall prices held steady over the quarter, the figures show varying trends across different housing types. Asking prices for three-bed semi-detached houses rose by €15,000 over the year to reach €295,000, marking a €5,000 increase in the last quarter alone. In contrast, four-bed semi-detached homes saw a yearly decrease of €5,500 to €359,500, despite experiencing a €7,000 quarterly rise.

Market availability improved locally, with 444 properties listed for sale across Limerick at the end of the third quarter, representing a 4 per cent increase over the period. Homes in the county are currently taking an average of just under three months to go sale agreed.

Commenting on the wider findings, Bank of Ireland Chief Economist Conall MacCoille said the report offers positive news for prospective buyers. "The rate of asking price inflation continues to slow, the number of properties for sale on MyHome is rising, and homebuilding has picked up. All of these factors point to positive news for homebuyers," he said. Nationally, MyHome Managing Director Joanne Geary noted a continued discrepancy between the first-time buyer and mover markets, with first-time buyer transactions up 12 per cent year-on-year while mover transactions fell slightly by 1.2 per cent.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.localAngle: The latest housing report details specific asking price trends and inventory levels for homes across Limerick city and county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362466.originalTitle: Limerick property prices continue to rise according to new report

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.headline: Big Shots Halloween Screams Film Competition Returns to Belltable on October 31
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.summary: Ireland’s All-Island Horror Film Competition is bringing its live screening, awards, and cash prizes to the Belltable on Saturday, October 31. Tickets for the Halloween night event cost €12.50, with doors opening at 6.30pm.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.story:
Horror filmmakers from across Ireland are gearing up for the return of Big Shots Halloween Screams to the Belltable on Saturday, October 31. Throughout the month of October, competing teams have been writing, shooting, and editing original short horror films to be showcased on the big screen.

The event, which follows previous successful editions in Limerick in 2024 and 2025, invites a live audience to view the finished entries. Attendees will also see various awards and cash prizes handed out to the standout productions of the night.

Doors at the O'Connell Street venue will open at 6.30pm ahead of the screenings, which are scheduled to kick off at 7.30pm. Tickets for the Halloween film event are priced at €12.50.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.localAngle: The annual horror film showcase returns to Limerick's Belltable venue, offering local film fans a live screening of original short movies on Halloween night.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362391.originalTitle: Big Shots Halloween Screams returns to Belltable for another night of frights

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.headline: Young Curators bring LASTA '26 festival to Belltable with film and variety show
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.summary: Co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca are bringing the youth-led LASTA '26 festival to Limerick's Belltable later this month, featuring a classic film screening and a multi-act variety show.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.story:
The Belltable is set to host two distinct events this month as part of LASTA ‘26, a national mentorship programme festival showcasing work made for and by young people. Co-curators Marcus Cropper and Ilinca Luca have put together the local programme to open up the venue as a space for creative experimentation and fun for their peers.

The festival opens on Wednesday, October 28, with screenings of the 1980 comedy classic 9 to 5 at 5pm and 7.30pm. Presented by Mr Cropper and Ms Luca in tribute to one of its performers, the film stars Dolly Parton, Lily Tomlin, and Jane Fonda as office workers who seek revenge on their sexist boss. Tickets are priced at €8, with concession tickets available for €5.

On Friday, October 30, at 7.30pm, the venue will host Nighttime Medley, a variety show featuring performances by Day Magee, Whimsy, and Limerick-based dance artist Alex Vostokova. The intimate stage show blends performance, drag clowning, and dance, with tickets costing €15 or €10.

Limerick-based artist Alex Vostokova, an Associate Artist at Dance Limerick, will perform Pit, a piece commissioned by CoisCéim Dance Theatre that explores public space and urbanism. The lineup also features Dublin-based artist Day Magee and drag clown performer Whimsy, known for appearances at Electric Picnic and The Outing.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.localAngle: The festival brings youth-led arts programming, including a performance by Limerick-based dance artist Alex Vostokova, directly to the Belltable stage.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362371.originalTitle: Young curators bring LASTA ‘26 to Belltable with film screening and variety show

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.headline: Limerick workers warned casual WhatsApp messages can be used as workplace evidence
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.summary: Local employment experts are warning Limerick workers and managers that informal WhatsApp messages and team chats can be used as official evidence in workplace disputes and investigations. Digital communications connected to colleagues are treated as professional conduct regardless of when or where they are sent.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.story:
Limerick employees and managers are being urged to exercise caution with digital communications as casual WhatsApp messages and team chat tools increasingly become formal workplace evidence. While messaging platforms offer a quick and efficient way to communicate, experts note that informal remarks or jokes sent in haste can look very different when reviewed during a workplace complaint or investigation.

A common issue in local workplace disputes involves screenshots of conversations circulating beyond small groups, highlighting that digital messages are rarely as private as users assume. Conversations that continue outside working hours or blur the line between professional and social topics still fall within the scope of workplace behaviour if they involve colleagues or work matters.

HR Hub, an employment law and human resource management firm based on O'Connell Street in Limerick, advises that employees should operate under the assumption that any message could eventually be seen by a wider audience. Managers carry an additional responsibility, as even informal messages can be interpreted as reflecting organisational views. Organisations are advised to establish clear expectations to ensure professional standards are maintained across all digital platforms.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.localAngle: The guidance was issued by Limerick-based human resource management and employment law experts HR Hub, operating from O’Connell Street.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362464.originalTitle: Employment Matters: When WhatsApp messages become workplace evidence

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.headline: Met Éireann issues dual weather warnings as Storm Boelo arrives in Limerick
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.summary: Status Yellow rain and wind warnings are in effect for Limerick as Storm Boelo brings heavy downpours and severe gusts. The county faces difficult travel conditions and possible structural damage.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.story:
Limerick is bracing for severe weather as Storm Boelo hits the county in the early hours of Saturday morning. Met Éireann has issued consecutive Status Yellow alerts for both rain and wind, warning locals of difficult travelling conditions, localized flooding, and potential disruption to outdoor events.

The rain warning takes effect at 4am on Saturday and runs until 3pm, to be immediately followed by a Status Yellow wind warning starting at 1pm and lasting until noon on Sunday. Forecasters have cautioned that severe and damaging gusts could cause structural damage to homes and businesses, alongside widespread delays to public transport.

Speaking on RTÉ’s Morning Ireland, Met Éireann senior forecaster Gerry Murphy noted that Storm Boelo differs in trajectory from Storm Austen, which passed over the country last Thursday. Heavy rain is expected to develop in the west after midnight and quickly sweep across the country, bringing wet and windy conditions throughout the weekend.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.localAngle: Limerick residents face hazardous travel and potential property damage as Status Yellow wind and rain warnings blanket the county for the weekend.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53113.originalTitle: Storm Boelo set to hit Limerick with high winds and heavy rain

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.headline: Limerick Chamber reveals shortlist for 15th annual Regional Business Awards
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.summary: Limerick Chamber has announced the finalists for its 15th annual Regional Business Awards, sponsored by TUS. Winners will be revealed at a gala dinner on November 13 at the Limerick Strand Hotel.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.story:
The finalists for the 15th annual Limerick Chamber Regional Business Awards have officially been named. Sponsored by the Technological University of the Shannon (TUS), the awards celebrate businesses across the Mid-West region ranging from emerging enterprises to established companies.

Limerick Chamber President Maria Gleeson praised the shortlisted organisations for their contributions to the region's success. "What stands out each year is the breadth of talent and enterprise across the Mid-West," she said. Liam Brown, Vice President at TUS, added that the awards provide an important platform to recognise the organisations shaping the future of the local economy.

The shortlist features competitive categories including Best Emerging Business, Best SME, Best Employer, Community Impact, Environmental Excellence, Customer Experience, Innovation and Digital Transformation, and Best Not-for-Profit Impact. Nominees include local names such as Fíor Jewellery, Croom Medical, Mother Macs, and the University Concert Hall.

The winners will be announced on Friday, November 13, at a gala dinner held at the Limerick Strand Hotel, attended by senior leaders from across the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362455.localAngle: The awards celebrate local businesses and enterprises driving economic and community success across Limerick and the wider Mid-West region.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.headline: Limerick Magician Steve Spade Channels Harry Houdini at Bunratty Castle Halloween Event
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.summary: Limerick master magician Steve Spade is headlining the bank holiday Halloween event at Bunratty Castle and Folk Park this weekend, recreating famous escapes exactly one century after Harry Houdini's passing.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.story:
Limerick master magician Steve Spade is bringing his homage to Harry Houdini to Bunratty Castle and Folk Park this bank holiday weekend, marking the centenary of the legendary escapologist's death. Spade, often called the Irish Houdini, owns a set of Houdini's own handcuffs after winning a rope-tie challenge on the Discovery Channel programme 'Baggage Battles'.

Speaking about his three-day appearance at the Co Clare venue, Spade confirmed he will perform live escapes alongside traditional parlour magic and host a question-and-answer session on Houdini's life and career. The Limerick magician's appearance is part of a broader commemoration, which also includes a private seance at Limerick's Studio Saol.

Visitors to Bunratty over the Halloween weekend will also encounter a range of spooky attractions, including the Human Spider illusion, Vera the Velociraptor, a Ghost Recruitment Bureau, a Wicked Wake, and a lively Witch Trial. Families can additionally enjoy apple bobbing in the Golden Vale and performances by international contortionist and juggler Frederico Fandango.

Spade's performances bridge local talent with international magic history, offering Limerick families a high-profile attraction just across the county border for the bank holiday weekend.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.localAngle: Limerick master magician Steve Spade is starring in the Bunratty Castle Halloween event, bringing his internationally recognised talents and Houdini memorabilia to a local audience.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362452.originalTitle: Spirit of Houdini will be one of the friendly ghosts to haunt Bunratty this weekend

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.headline: Limerick Psychotherapist Warns CORU Fast-Track Training Puts Vulnerable at Risk
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.summary: Limerick psychotherapist Trish Murphy has warned that CORU's proposed fast-track training regulations could fail vulnerable people. The Irish Council for Psychotherapy argues the changes dilute standards by cutting supervision and personal therapy requirements.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.story:
A Limerick psychotherapist has warned that proposed new training regulations aimed at clearing mental health waiting lists could put vulnerable people at risk. Trish Murphy, a Limerick native and Director of Student Counselling Services at Trinity College Dublin, issued the warning following her organisation's annual conference.

Ms Murphy echoed concerns raised by the Irish Council for Psychotherapy (ICP) regarding new standards of proficiency suggested by health professionals regulatory body CORU. The proposed changes would introduce a shorter training period while dropping requirements for personal therapy and supervision, alongside a reduced focus on the therapeutic relationship.

"Newly trained psychotherapists will not be equipped to provide the relational capacity that is essential to the long-term processing of trauma when treating the most vulnerable children, adolescents, and adult clients," Ms Murphy said.

Rúaidhrí O’Connor, CEO of the ICP, criticized the regulatory body for failing to consult directly with professional representative bodies between December 2023 and July 2025. The ICP is urging CORU to engage with the profession to ensure public protection remains central to regulatory decisions.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.localAngle: The warning was issued by Limerick-native Trish Murphy, a qualified psychotherapist and Director of Student Counselling Services at Trinity College Dublin, following her organization's annual conference.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362447.originalTitle: Limerick psychotherapist warns of dangers of fast-track training

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362395.headline: Internationally Acclaimed Pianist Yeol Eum Son to Perform Mozart at UCH
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362395.summary: South Korean pianist Yeol Eum Son will perform with the Irish Chamber Orchestra at the University Concert Hall on Friday, November 20. The 'Mozart Illuminated' concert begins at 7.30pm as part of a three-date Irish tour.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362395.story:
Music fans across the 061 are in for a treat next month as renowned South Korean pianist Yeol Eum Son brings her upcoming Irish tour to the University Concert Hall (UCH). 

Taking place on Friday, November 20 at 7.30pm, the concert is titled 'Mozart Illuminated' and will feature Son performing as both soloist and director alongside the Irish Chamber Orchestra (ICO). The Limerick performance is part of a three-date national tour that also visits Dublin and Cork.

Limerick audiences will see Son perform Mozart’s much-loved "Elvira Madigan" concerto (Piano Concerto No. 21) alongside the dramatic Piano Concerto No. 24 in C minor. The evening's programme will open with Mozart's Divertimento in D major, directed by ICO guest leader Hed Yaron Meyerson.

Son is widely recognised for her international performing career, including a recent sold-out BBC Proms performance at the Royal Albert Hall. Her famous 2011 performance of Mozart’s Piano Concerto No. 21 has garnered over 32 million online views. Tickets for the Limerick concert are available directly from the Irish Chamber Orchestra website.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362395.localAngle: The concert brings a world-renowned classical music performance directly to Limerick's University Concert Hall as part of an exclusive three-date Irish tour.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362395.originalTitle: From BBC Proms to the ICO: Yeol Eum Son brings Mozart to UCH

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362479.headline: New Horror Film 'Bloody Tennis' Fails to Score in 2/5 Review
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362479.summary: Nikias Chryssos's new horror-thriller 'Bloody Tennis' has received a disappointing two-star review after failing to deliver on its ambitious premise. The film follows an American teen at a brutal elite tennis academy in Southern Europe.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362479.story:
Film critics have delivered a fault to new horror-thriller 'Bloody Tennis', panning the movie as an underdeveloped and unpleasant entry into the cannibalistic horror sub-genre. Directed by Nikias Chryssos, the film opens with American student Sophie, played by Sandra Guldberg, arriving at an elite tennis academy in Southern Europe.

While initially drawing comparisons to 'Suspiria', the film quickly shifts into 'Saw' and 'Raw' territory as Sophie navigates a twisted bootcamp for aspiring tennis stars. However, reviewers noted that the movie struggles to build momentum, offering a half-hearted body count and weak-kneed attempts at man-eating horror.

Critics also pointed to surreal clay court bouts and catfighting that ultimately overlook tension, leaving audiences with a disjointed narrative and an unsatisfying grand finale. Earning a lacklustre two-star rating, the film proves that even with high stakes on the court, this particular match lacks any real love.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362479.localAngle: Local film enthusiasts looking for their next cinema trip may want to skip this poorly received sports-horror crossover when it hits screens.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362492.headline: UHL Cancer Partnership Wins National Award for Community-Based Treatment
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362492.summary: A Limerick cancer care service that brings treatments closer to patients' homes won a national award at the HSE Integrated Healthcare Conference, following nearly 10,000 interventions delivered across the Mid West last year.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362492.story:
A collaborative healthcare initiative that delivers cancer treatments directly to communities across Limerick and the Mid West has been recognised nationally, winning an award at the recent HSE Integrated Healthcare Conference.

The partnership between University Hospital Limerick (UHL) Cancer Services and the regional Community Intervention Team (CIT) allows patients to receive oncology care locally rather than travelling to the hospital. Operating seven days a week from hubs including Limerick, Newcastle West, Ennis, Nenagh, and Thurles, the nurse-led service carried out nearly 10,000 community oncology interventions in 2025. Services range from blood tests and chemotherapy pump disconnections to managing central venous access devices and supporting palliative care.

Minister for Health highlighted the regional initiative as a model that could be replicated across the country. Áine Collins, oncology clinical nurse manager, praised the collaboration between hospital and community services.

"Patients can experience significant vulnerability throughout their cancer journey, and the kindness, compassion and professionalism demonstrated by the CIT staff makes a real difference," she said. "The consistently positive feedback from patients and their families is a strong testament to the quality of care provided."
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362492.localAngle: The award-winning service operates directly out of Limerick and Newcastle West hubs, cutting down travel times for local patients and freeing up hospital capacity at UHL.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362492.originalTitle: Cancer care brought closer to home in Mid West

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53174.headline: Gardaí Catch Drivers Doing 139km/h on Limerick Roads During Bank Holiday Operation
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53174.summary: Motorists were clocked traveling at 121km/h and 139km/h on Limerick roads yesterday as Gardaí ramp up checkpoints for the October bank holiday weekend. Across the country, 77 people have been arrested for driving under the influence and over 2,300 drivers caught speeding.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53174.story:
Motorists in Limerick were caught significantly exceeding speed limits yesterday as part of an ongoing national Garda Roads Policing operation over the October bank holiday weekend.

On the R520 in Newcastlewest, a driver was recorded travelling at 121km/h in an 80km/h zone. Meanwhile, on the N18 in Ballinacurra Weston, a vehicle was clocked at 139km/h in a 100km/h zone.

The operation, which began on Thursday, October 22, includes statutory Mandatory Intoxicant Testing checkpoints alongside high-visibility patrols. Nationally, three days into the campaign, Gardaí have detected 2,311 speeding offences and arrested 77 people for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Additionally, over 250 drivers were caught using mobile phones or failing to wear seatbelts.

With two fatal collisions occurring on Irish roads since the operation started—bringing the national death toll to 153 for the year—An Garda Síochána and the Road Safety Authority are urging all road users to exercise caution. Gardaí have issued a warning to slow down, avoid intoxicants, wear seatbelts, and stay off mobile devices. The enforcement operation will continue across the county until Tuesday, October 27.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53174.localAngle: Local motorists were clocked speeding significantly over the limit in Newcastlewest and Ballinacurra Weston as part of a nationwide bank holiday Garda clampdown.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53174.originalTitle: High speeds detected on two Limerick roads yesterday

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362490.headline: Limerick Issued 1,970 Footpath Parking Fines But Just Four Dog Fouling Penalties
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362490.summary: New national data reveals a massive disparity in enforcement across Limerick last year, with thousands of motorists penalized for blocking footpaths while only four fines were handed out for dog fouling.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362490.story:
Limerick motorists faced nearly 2,000 penalties for parking on footpaths last year, while dog owners received just four fines for fouling across the city and county, according to figures released by Vision Ireland.

The stark contrast highlights the vast difference in local enforcement between the two issues. Across the entire country, just 44 dog fouling fines were issued last year, compared to a staggering 21,352 fines for parking on footpaths.

The data was compiled as part of Vision Ireland’s ongoing 'Clear Our Paths' campaign, which aims to raise awareness about the daily obstacles and hazards faced by people with vision impairments navigating public walkways.

While Limerick recorded just four dog fouling fines, County Kerry led the country in that category with 12. Meanwhile, the highest number of footpath parking fines nationwide was recorded by Dublin City Council at 4,833.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362490.localAngle: Limerick recorded 1,970 footpath parking fines compared to only four dog fouling penalties last year, according to national data highlighting accessibility barriers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362490.originalTitle: Fines for parking on footpaths and dog fouling on equal playing field

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362487.headline: Lumen Street Theatre Brings Spooky Halloween Events to Rathkeale
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362487.summary: Rathkeale will host two Halloween events organised by Lumen Street Theatre on October 30 and 31, featuring a pumpkin patch, a parade, and fancy-dress competitions.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362487.story:
Rathkeale is preparing for a weekend of Halloween celebrations as Lumen Street Theatre brings two major events to the town on October 30 and 31.

The festivities kick off on Friday, October 30, with the 'Dullahan to Darkness: Halloween Pumpkin Patch' at The Greenway Hub, running from 4pm to 8pm. Attendees can take part in pumpkin carving, listen to storytelling, and experience a Ghost Rider feature, alongside complimentary pumpkin soup and hot chocolate. Tickets for the opening event are available on Eventbrite.

The celebrations continue on Saturday, October 31, with the 'Dullahan to Darkness Childcatcher Halloween Parade'. Gathering begins at the Rathkeale House Hotel at 6pm, with the procession officially setting off at 7pm. Prizes will be awarded for the best costumes during the parade.

Following the procession, local celebrations will move to Manns for an adult fancy-dress disco starting at 10pm, which will also feature additional costume prizes. Both events have been entirely created and produced by Lumen Street Theatre.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362487.localAngle: The events bring festive community celebrations and entertainment directly to the West Limerick town of Rathkeale for the Halloween weekend.

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53167.headline: UL Graduate Aideen Howard to Represent Ireland at Miss Universe
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53167.summary: Recent University of Limerick graduate Aideen Howard will represent Ireland at the Miss Universe pageant in Puerto Rico this November, following her crowning in Dublin earlier this year.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53167.story:
A freshly minted University of Limerick graduate is preparing for the international stage after being named Miss Universe Ireland. Aideen Howard will travel to Puerto Rico at the end of November for the global championship, marking a whirlwind transition from campus life to the world of international pageantry.

Born in Boston but raised in Limerick from the age of 12, Howard embraces her dual heritage. Reflecting on her move to Ireland as a child, she recalled feeling conscious of standing out, offering advice to her younger self to be patient and trust the process. That journey ultimately led her to the Bonnington Hotel in Dublin on June 20, where she was crowned Miss Universe Ireland.

"The first thing I did was look over at my friends and family, and I was just so excited to get over to them and hug them," Howard said of the surreal moment her name was called. "And then it actually hit me, I’m Miss Universe Ireland. It was just such a special moment I’ll remember for the rest of life."

Beyond the visual elements of the competition, Howard aims to challenge common misconceptions about pageants. She emphasizes that the role requires strong communication skills, confidence under pressure, and the ability to represent something larger than oneself. Juggling exams and assignments just months ago, she now looks forward to making her home country proud on the global stage.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53167.localAngle: Raised in Limerick after moving from Boston at age 12, the University of Limerick graduate carries her local roots to the international stage in Puerto Rico.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53167.originalTitle: University of Limerick graduate to represent Ireland at Miss Universe

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362482.headline: Limerick Homebuyers Face Costly Repairs After Concealed Attic Leak Discovered
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362482.summary: A Limerick homeowner left with substantial repair bills following a major attic leak six months after purchase is advised to check insurance policies and examine potential grounds for professional negligence or misrepresentation.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362482.story:
Buying a home across Limerick comes with significant financial and emotional investment, but one local property owner has found themselves facing sizeable repair bills and damaged belongings just six months after moving in. A substantial leak originating from the attic revealed what appears to be a quick 'patch' job carried out by the previous owner prior to the sale.

Despite having a pre-purchase survey conducted that disclosed no problems, the homeowner is now grappling with the fallout while the surveyor has maintained that everything appeared fine during the initial inspection. Under standard property transactions governed by the principle of caveat emptor, or "buyer beware", vendors generally have no duty to disclose physical defects and offer no guarantees.

However, legal experts note that this principle does not permit a seller to deliberately conceal serious problems or make false statements, which could open grounds for a misrepresentation claim. Additionally, homeowners facing similar situations must examine their surveyor's responsibilities, as a professional negligence claim could be considered if a competent inspector should have reasonably identified the evidence of a previous repair.

As an immediate step, affected buyers are advised to contact their home insurance provider to check for policy coverage, take photos of the damage, and have a qualified professional inspect the leak to establish its cause and whether previous patch work was evident.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362482.localAngle: This property dispute highlights the hidden legal and financial risks facing house hunters navigating the local housing market across Limerick.

The new issue forms part of a wider six-stamp collection capturing the origins and history of cities including Dublin, Cork, Galway, Kilkenny, and Waterford. Designed by Donegal-based heraldic artist Philip Mackey, the stamps are valued at the 'N' rate of €1.85 to cover domestic postage.

The stamps are available now in sheetlets of four online, at local post offices in the featured cities, and at selected locations nationwide.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362501.headline: Gardaí Issue Fraud Warning After Limerick Women Targetted in Phone Scams
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362501.summary: Limerick Gardaí are urging the public to protect their financial details following two separate telephone scams, including one where a woman in her 70s was defrauded of money.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362501.story:
Gardaí in Limerick have issued a stark warning against sharing bank or credit card details over the phone following two recent fraudulent incidents in the county.

According to the Crime Prevention Office, a woman in her seventies received a call claiming her Visa card had been hacked and money stolen from her account. She was instructed to download an app and transfer funds, complying with the directions before growing suspicious when a further payment was demanded. In a separate incident in Caherconlish, another woman handed over her Visa debit card details and security code after receiving a call from someone falsely claiming to represent her internet service provider, resulting in unauthorized transfers from her account.

Sergeant Michelle O’Halloran warned that fraudsters frequently rely on creating panic and pressure to force quick decisions. “Be suspicious of unexpected calls claiming there is a problem with your bank account, card or internet service,” Sgt O’Halloran said, reminding the public never to disclose PINs, passwords, one-time passcodes, or security details to unexpected callers.

Gardaí emphasize that legitimate banks will never ask customers to transfer money to a supposedly safe account or direct them to download an app to protect funds. Anyone who receives a suspicious call is advised to hang up immediately and contact their bank directly using a trusted number from an official website or bank card, and to report any financial losses to Gardaí without delay.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362501.localAngle: Local Gardaí across Limerick are warning residents to remain vigilant against telephone fraudsters targeting bank accounts and personal details in the area.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362514.headline: Shannon Airport hotel ordered to pay €25,000 for age discrimination
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362514.summary: The Workplace Relations Commission has ordered CG Hotels Limited to pay a long-serving food and beverage assistant €25,000 after he was dismissed upon turning 66.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362514.story:
The operator of a Shannon Airport-based hotel has been ordered to pay a long-serving worker €25,000 in compensation after he was unlawfully discriminated against on the grounds of age.

Rajamohan Pillay, who worked as a Food and Beverage Assistant at the Park Inn by Radisson Shannon Airport since 2011, brought his case to the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC). Adjudicator Ewa Sobanska ruled that Mr Pillay was dismissed from his employment on January 12, 2025, when CG Hotels Limited refused to extend his contract past his 66th birthday. Representing himself at the hearing, Mr Pillay stated he had a mortgage to pay for another five years, felt fit and healthy, and did not want to retire.

In its defence, CG Hotels Ltd argued that Mr Pillay had reached the firm’s normal contractual retirement age of 65 in January 2024, maintaining that his subsequent dismissal was without foundation. However, Ms Sobanska found that there was no cogent evidence put forward to show that the mandatory retirement age had been clearly communicated to the employee.

While noting that employers can stipulate a fixed retirement age or offer fixed-term contracts to older workers, Ms Sobanska ruled that such measures must be objectively and reasonably justified by a legitimate aim. Under Section 77 of the Employment Equality Act 1998, she ordered the hotel operator to pay Mr Pillay the equivalent of one year’s net wages.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362514.localAngle: The ruling impacts employment practices at a major hotel operating at Shannon Airport in the Mid-West region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362514.originalTitle: Shannon hotel ordered to pay €25,000 to worker who claimed discrimination on age grounds

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53192.headline: Hermitage Green to Support Robbie Williams at Thomond Park in July 2027
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53192.summary: Limerick band Hermitage Green will play two massive homecoming concerts in July 2027, opening for international pop star Robbie Williams at Thomond Park. The milestone comes 16 years after the five-piece ensemble played their very first gig at the Curragower Bar.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53192.story:
Limerick five-piece band Hermitage Green are preparing for one of the biggest performances of their career, securing a support slot for Robbie Williams at Thomond Park for two concerts in July 2027. 

For frontman Barry Murphy, the upcoming stadium shows mark a remarkable full-circle journey. Growing up across the road from the stadium, Murphy listened to gigs from his bedroom window and was a devoted fan of the British singer, receiving his album 'Life Thru a Lens' as a child. Years later, the former Munster rugby player will share the stage with his childhood idol at the very same venue where he once scored a try against the All Blacks.

Formed in 2010 through casual jam sessions at the Curragower Bar just down the road from Thomond Park, the band has since built an international following, releasing charting EPs and albums like 'Save Your Soul' through Sony Music Ireland. Despite touring across Europe, North America, and the Middle East, the band maintains deep roots in Limerick.

Murphy expressed his excitement for the homecoming performance, noting that playing in front of his hometown crowd alongside his childhood hero will likely top any venue they have played around the world.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53192.localAngle: The band formed in a Limerick pub 16 years ago and the frontman grew up across the road from Thomond Park, where they will now support Robbie Williams.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362508.headline: Treaty United operator records €1m loss as club prepares for Limerick FC rebrand
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362508.summary: The firm operating Limerick City's League of Ireland club recorded post-tax losses of nearly €1 million last year, bringing its accumulated losses to €2.13 million. The club recently finished its final campaign as Treaty United and will be renamed Limerick FC next season.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362508.story:
Recently filed accounts lodged with the Companies Office by Treaty Utd Ltd show post-tax losses of €998,603 for 2025, following losses of €839,258 the previous year. By the end of December, the firm's accumulated losses stood at €2.13 million, while the amount owed to group undertakings increased from €1.22 million to €2.22 million.

The financial figures emerge as the club prepares for a significant transition. Treaty United played its final League of Ireland fixture at the weekend—a 2-0 victory over Cobh Ramblers—to finish second from bottom in the Men’s First Division. The club is set to be officially renamed Limerick FC ahead of the upcoming season.

A note attached to the accounts, signed off by Harold (Scott) Fraser and Charles (Chuck) Cosman, indicates that the company remains loss-making in 2026. The filing notes that the business relies on existing cash facilities, investor loans, and ongoing financial backing from key shareholder Treaty Football Holdings Inc. The shareholder has confirmed it will not seek loan repayments for at least 12 months and will continue to provide necessary operational support while new management implements its business plan.

Founded in 2020, Treaty United saw its women's team enter the Premier Division that year before the men's team secured a First Division licence in 2021. The club was subsequently acquired by former Ireland international Ciara McCormack in partnership with a Canadian-based investment group led by Tricor Pacific Capital Inc. A spokesman for Treaty Utd declined to comment when contacted regarding the accounts.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362508.localAngle: The financial update impacts Limerick City's primary League of Ireland soccer club as it prepares to rebrand as Limerick FC for the upcoming season.

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53190.summary: Templeglantine overcame an eight-point second-half deficit in Adare, clinching the Limerick intermediate camogie title with a dramatic injury-time goal from Noelle Curtin.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53190.story:
Templeglantine staged a remarkable comeback to claim the Limerick intermediate camogie title in Adare, erasing an eight-point deficit against Na Piarsaigh in the closing minutes of the game.

Na Piarsaigh had led from the opening score and held a 1-07 to 0-04 advantage at half-time, aided by a gale-force wind. They extended their lead further when Rosie McCaul fired into the top right corner with under ten minutes remaining, leaving Pat McInerney's side trailing by eight points. However, Stephanie Woulfe kept Templeglantine in touch throughout with reliable free-taking, scoring seven frees and one from play.

The West Limerick side launched a devastating response late in the game, outscoring their opponents by two goals and five points to just one score. The decisive blow arrived in injury time when Noelle Curtin found the bottom left corner to seal the victory.

Manager Pat McInerney praised his side's fitness and determination after the final whistle, crediting their demanding training sessions. Player of the match Shauna Quinlivan was recognised before captain Connie Sheehan lifted the cup, with the club now advancing to Munster Championship action next weekend ahead of senior status next year.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362512.headline: Shannon Foynes Port Company Posts Record €17.5M Profit and Surging Tonnage
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362512.summary: Shannon Foynes Port Company has reported a record-breaking 12 per cent profit increase to €17.5 million, driven by strong performance at its Limerick and Foynes terminals.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362512.story:
Shannon Foynes Port Company (SFPC) has recorded a record-breaking profit of 12 per cent to just over €17.5m, bolstered by significant revenue growth across its directly managed and privately owned terminals.

The company posted an EBITDA of more than €8m for the first time, alongside a record operating profit of €5.71m, up from €4.81m in 2024. Ship and cargo revenues increased by 10.1 per cent, while total throughput across the Shannon Estuary rose 2.2 per cent to 9.35m tonnes. Foynes Port, the company's largest terminal, achieved its highest-ever annual tonnage with a 10.8 per cent year-on-year increase, ending the period with net assets of €72m.

Chief Executive Officer Pat Keating attributed the financial success to a focus on revenue growth, cost management, and maximizing asset capacity at the Foynes and Limerick terminals. He noted that the results underline the port's expanding role in regional and national supply chains.

Looking ahead under Vision 2041, SFPC is advancing plans for the Foynes Island Deepwater Port and enhanced connectivity. The 40km Limerick to Foynes rail line is scheduled to reopen for freight services in the first quarter of 2027, which is expected to significantly boost national freight modal shift.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362512.localAngle: The financial milestone highlights the growing economic and logistical importance of the Limerick and Foynes port terminals to the regional supply chain.

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53234.headline: Gardaí issue Limerick Halloween warning after powerful new fireworks seized on black market
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53234.summary: An Garda Síochána has issued a public safety appeal across Limerick and nationwide ahead of Halloween following the discovery of powerful new illegal fireworks. Authorities have seized 575 fireworks worth over €235,000 under Operation Tombola between 2023 and 2026.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53234.story:
Gardaí have issued a public safety appeal ahead of Halloween following the discovery of powerful new fireworks on the black market. The warning comes as Operation Tombola, An Garda Síochána’s annual campaign aimed at preventing the importation, sale and use of illegal fireworks, continues across the country.

According to Gardaí, 575 fireworks worth an estimated €235,163 have been seized under Operation Tombola between 2023 and 2026, with seizures increasing by 7% in 2026 compared to the previous year. The operation seeks to raise awareness of legislation prohibiting the import, sale, and possession of fireworks, while highlighting the dangers of burns, injuries, fires, and distress caused to vulnerable community members and animals.

Figures released by Gardaí indicate that over 98% of recorded incidents were categorized as firework offences. Of those incidents involving a suspected offender, 95% were male, 5% were female, and 71% were under the age of 18. Authorities are urging the public to enjoy Halloween responsibly, advising parents to supervise children near bonfires and to only attend organized public events.

Gardaí also reminded the public to consider older residents, individuals with sensory issues, and animals who can experience severe stress and anxiety from fireworks. Officials advised people never to handle or throw fireworks, and never to consume intoxicants near bonfires.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53234.localAngle: The nationwide Garda safety campaign and crackdown on illegal fireworks directly impacts local communities across Limerick ahead of Halloween celebrations.

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53229.headline: UL Student Life Launches Inclusive SHAG Week Promoting Safe Sex and Wellbeing
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53229.summary: The University of Limerick has kicked off its annual Sexual Health and Guidance Week, featuring queer-inclusive events, STI testing, and wellness workshops running until Thursday.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53229.story:
The University of Limerick’s Student Life has launched its annual Sexual Health and Guidance (SHAG) Week, running until Thursday, October 29. The programme aims to provide students with an open and inclusive platform to learn about sex, relationships, and wellbeing as they navigate new experiences on campus.

Cuán Hayes, Vice President for Diversity and Inclusion in UL Student Life, noted that college is often the first space where young people freely explore their sexual identities. "There’s a lot of people having sex, and it’s nice to see they’re using protection, but SHAG Week is about elevating that message of safety, because students are going to have sex no matter what," Hayes said. Events include a Sex Fair at the Student Centre featuring games and prizes, alongside an information seminar hosted by Sex Siopa.

Organisers have this year shifted away from gender-segregated programming, such as previous sections titled 'Viva la Vulva' and 'Penis Power', bringing all activities under a single, queer- and trans-inclusive umbrella. Collaborations with local organisations include on-campus STI testing provided by GOSHH (Gender, Orientation, Sexual Health and HIV) and resources on gender-affirming care from the Trans Limerick Community (TLC).

Students seeking information or resources can access pamphlets and events on campus or view details via the UL Student Life Instagram page. Hayes encouraged all students to participate, noting that confidential resources and support are available for those who prefer to browse independently.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53229.localAngle: The event is hosted on campus by University of Limerick Student Life in partnership with local Limerick organisations GOSHH and the Trans Limerick Community.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53229.originalTitle: UL’s SHAG Week will provide a more inclusive sexual health platform for students

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53201.headline: England striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or with roots in Caherline
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53201.summary: England captain Harry Kane has won football's prestigious Ballon d'Or award. The striker's paternal grandmother was born in Caherline, County Limerick, and he is also a descendant of a 1897 All-Ireland winning hurler.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53201.story:
England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has been awarded the Ballon d’Or following a stellar career that has seen him score 543 goals to date. While celebrations took place in London, supporters in the Treaty County can also claim a connection to football's highest individual honour.

Kane's paternal grandmother, Teresa Fitzgerald, was born in Caherline, just outside Caherconlish, before she emigrated to Britain during the 1950s. His grandfather, Mike Kane, originally hailed from County Galway.

The 33-year-old's Limerick lineage extends further into sporting history. Kane is a descendant of Jim Flood, a member of the Limerick team that defeated Kilkenny to secure the county's first All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship in 1897.

Having netted 156 goals in 159 appearances for Bayern Munich alongside his record-breaking spells for Tottenham Hotspur and England, Kane's family history provides Treaty County fans with a unique local link to a global football star.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53201.localAngle: Harry Kane's paternal grandmother was born in Caherline and he is a descendant of 1897 All-Ireland hurling winner Jim Flood.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53201.originalTitle: Caherline’s claim to Ballon D’or: Harry Kane’s unlikely Limerick link

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362543.headline: Limerick Council Rolls Out Communication Boards Across 16 County Libraries
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362543.summary: Following a query from Social Democrats Councillor Shane Hickey-O'Mara, Limerick City and County Council confirmed that new communication boards have been delivered, wall-mounted, and distributed to all 16 library branches across the county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362543.story:
New communication boards have been successfully rolled out across all 16 library branches in Limerick city and county, local authority officials have confirmed.

The update was provided following a query from Social Democrats councillor Shane Hickey-O’Mara, who had asked the Council for details regarding the procurement, timeline, and rollout of the accessibility tools in local authority-run spaces.

In response, the Council revealed that relevant charity organisations were consulted during the process. Product samples were subsequently reviewed, leading to an order being placed to meet the anticipated needs of the library service.

The selected communication boards have now been delivered and distributed across all 16 branches. The local authority confirmed that wall-mounted signs have been installed, alongside A4 laminated boards designed for individuals of different abilities to use.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362543.localAngle: The new accessibility boards have been installed in all 16 library branches across Limerick city and county.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362543.originalTitle: Update sought on communication boards in Limerick council ran spaces

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362541.headline: Limerick City and County Council seizes abandoned horse in John Carew Park
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362541.summary: Limerick City and County Council has seized an abandoned 1.5-year-old horse in the John Carew Park area of the city. The animal will be re-homed outside of Limerick if not claimed within five days.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362541.story:
Limerick City and County Council has removed an abandoned horse from a busy residential area in Limerick City.

According to a statement from the local authority, the 1.5-year-old brown and white male horse was seized on October 6 at Collivet Court in John Carew Park. 

The Council confirmed that the owners or keepers of the animal are currently unknown. Under local procedures, seized horses that remain unclaimed after a five-day period are re-homed to shelters outside of Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362541.localAngle: The incident involves the removal of an abandoned animal from a residential neighbourhood in Limerick City by the local authority.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362539.headline: Cllr Elena Secas calls for dedicated Bus Éireann office in Limerick
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362539.summary: Independent Councillor Elena Secas is pushing for a dedicated Bus Éireann communication office in Limerick to resolve ongoing delays faced by parents dealing with school transport queries.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362539.story:
Independent Councillor Elena Secas has called for the establishment of a dedicated Bus Éireann communication office in Limerick. The City East representative raised the issue following persistent difficulties experienced by local parents trying to contact the transport provider regarding school transport queries.

According to Cllr Secas, families are currently forced to deal exclusively with the main Bus Éireann office in Dublin, with no direct contact route available for the Limerick branch. She stated that repeated phone calls, emails, and online forms are frequently left unanswered for weeks at a time.

"This lack of communication makes it extremely difficult to support families and resolve problems in a timely manner," Cllr Secas said, adding that the delays carry serious consequences for local households and cause widespread frustration.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362539.localAngle: The proposed communication office would directly benefit Limerick families struggling to resolve school transport issues with the national provider.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362539.originalTitle: Dedicated Bus Éireann communication office on Cllr wishlist

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362547.headline: Limerick District League kick off Oscar Traynor campaign with 5-2 win over Desmond League
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362547.summary: John Lysaght's Limerick side secured a 5-2 away victory against the Desmond League at Mick Hanly Park in Askeaton on Wednesday. Goals from Joel Coustrain, Filip Mostowy, Vinny Ryan, and James Fitzgerald got the campaign off to a winning start.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362547.story:
The Limerick District League made a winning start to their Oscar Traynor Trophy campaign this week, securing a 5-2 away victory over the Desmond League at Mick Hanly Park in Askeaton.

Managed by John Lysaght, the Limerick team found the net five times mid-week to claim the opening points in a group phase that also features Cork and North Tipperary.

The goals came courtesy of a brace from Aisling Annacotty's Joel Coustrain, alongside strikes from Filip Mostowy of Regional United, Ballynanty Rovers player Vinny Ryan, and James Fitzgerald of Geraldines.

Limerick will be looking to build on this strong opening performance as they aim to capture the competition outright for the first time since 2019.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.headline: Abbeyfeale Homeowners Targeted as Thieves Siphon Heating Oil From Vacant Property
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.summary: Gardaí in Abbeyfeale have launched an investigation after thieves siphoned home heating oil from a property left vacant for two weeks. Authorities have issued a security warning to homeowners across Limerick as colder weather arrives.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.story:
Gardaí in Abbeyfeale are investigating the theft of home heating oil from a local property after thieves targeted a house that had been vacant for just two weeks. When the homeowners returned to the premises, they discovered that the oil had been siphoned directly from their tank.

In response to the incident, Crime Prevention Officer Sergeant Michelle O’Halloran has issued a timely warning to residents across Limerick as temperatures begin to drop. She urged homeowners to ensure their oil tanks are properly secured ahead of the winter months.

"If possible, consider installing a lockable tank cover or security cage, and make sure the tank is positioned in a secure and well-lit area," Sergeant O’Halloran said. She added that external lighting, CCTV systems, and house alarms can also serve as effective deterrents against fuel theft.

Authorities have also advised residents who plan on leaving their homes vacant for any period of time to ask a trusted neighbour to keep a watchful eye on the property and immediately report any suspicious activity to local Gardaí.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.localAngle: The incident occurred at a property in Abbeyfeale, prompting local Gardaí to issue a winter security warning for homeowners across Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362545.originalTitle: Limerick Gardaí warn of theft of home heating oil as colder months set in

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.headline: Limerick Dementia Social Club Announces Autumn and Winter Programme of Activities
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.summary: The Limerick Dementia Social Club has released its upcoming schedule of events at Our Lady of Lourdes Community Centre on Childers Road, offering music, choirs, and support sessions for people living with dementia and their carers.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.story:
The Limerick Dementia Social Club has announced its new schedule of activities for the coming months, offering a regular meeting space for people living with dementia and their carers on the first Wednesday of every month.

Held at Our Lady of Lourdes Community Centre on Childers Road from 6.30pm to 8.45pm, the club aims to provide a non-judgemental space to socialise and combat isolation. Established in 2018 by Mags O’Sullivan and her co-workers, the initiative connects members with local performers, including a planned ‘Fleming Ball’ and a ‘Craic agus Ceol’ session on Wednesday, November 4. Professional music therapist Cathy McGlynn also leads the ‘Melodies Memory Choir’ every third Wednesday.

Ms O’Sullivan noted the profound impact of music on attendees, particularly those experiencing communication difficulties. "We have people in the club that have difficulty with communication and expressive language, yet when we sing together, they may remember a whole verse of a song," she said. In addition to music, monthly gatherings feature guest speakers providing practical advice on nutrition, mobility, and care strategies for carers.

The club will host a Christmas Festive Evening and fundraiser with a raffle and spot prizes on Wednesday, December 2. Anyone seeking further information on the upcoming schedule can contact Mags O’Sullivan via email at limerickdementiasc@gmail.com.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.localAngle: The club provides vital social and support services for dementia patients and their carers at Our Lady of Lourdes Community Centre on Childers Road.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53246.originalTitle: Music and community at the heart of Limerick Dementia Social Club this season

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.headline: Gardaí seize €644,000 of cocaine and heroin during Old Singland Road search
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.summary: Limerick Gardaí arrested a woman in her 40s after uncovering €490,000 of cocaine and €154,000 of heroin at a residential property on Wednesday.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.story:
Gardaí in Limerick have seized a significant quantity of illegal drugs with an estimated street value of €644,000 following a search on the city's east side.

Officers attached to the Limerick Divisional Drug Unit carried out the search under warrant at a residential property on Old Singland Road on Wednesday, October 28. During the operation, which formed part of an ongoing targeted campaign against drug distribution in the Mid-West region, officers uncovered €490,000 worth of cocaine alongside €154,000 of heroin.

A woman aged in her 40s was arrested at the scene in connection with the intelligence-led seizure. She is currently being held in Garda custody in the Limerick area under the provisions of Section 2 of the Criminal Justice Act 1996.

Gardaí have confirmed that the investigation remains ongoing as officers continue to target the supply of controlled substances across the region.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362602.localAngle: The major drugs seizure took place at a residential property on Old Singland Road as part of an operation targeting criminal networks across the Mid-West.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.headline: Limerick Bus Drivers Targeted as Fireworks Thrown into Vehicles Ahead of Halloween
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.summary: Bus services in Limerick, including the 303 and Expressway Route 13, have faced temporary suspensions after gangs threw fireworks into vehicles, terrifying passengers and drivers.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.story:
Bus drivers operating in parts of Limerick are facing dangerous conditions in the run-up to Halloween, with gangs of youths throwing fireworks directly into vehicles. The disruption has forced the temporary suspension of certain services, predominantly impacting the 303 route between Pineview and Kilmallock Road, as well as Expressway Route 13 connecting Limerick and Tralee.

Aontú Councillor Sarah Beasley said drivers have contacted her at their wits' end. One driver reported that a firework exploded inside a bus, leaving an elderly passenger terrified. Cllr Beasley noted that drivers are naturally reluctant to enter certain estates after dark, resulting in significant inconvenience for regular public transport users who rely on the services.

Bus Éireann confirmed that services have experienced recent anti-social behaviour and will be curtailed wherever there is a risk to safety. Additional security has been arranged across Limerick for the Halloween period, and the company is liaising closely with An Garda Síochána. Officials have also reiterated that the possession, sale, or use of unlicensed fireworks is illegal, carrying penalties of up to €10,000 in fines and five years in prison.

The recent transport incidents follow an earlier occurrence this month on the 303 route, where child vandals concealed Stanley-type blades in bus seats, causing extensive damage to the upholstery and putting passengers at serious risk.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.localAngle: Public transport routes across Limerick City and surrounding areas are experiencing severe disruptions and safety hazards due to anti-social behaviour ahead of Halloween.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362583.originalTitle: Limerick bus drivers “terrorised” in run up to Halloween

https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.headline: Limerick striker Ronan Coughlan helps Fleetwood Town knock Arsenal out of Carabao Cup
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.summary: Limerick-born Ronan Coughlan scored in a penalty shootout as League Two side Fleetwood Town pulled off a shock Carabao Cup win against Premier League champions Arsenal.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.story:
Limerick native Ronan Coughlan played a pivotal role on Tuesday night as Fleetwood Town pulled off a major upset, eliminating Premier League champions Arsenal from the Carabao Cup at Highbury Stadium.

The 30-year-old striker stepped up to score the first penalty in a 5-3 shootout victory after the match ended 1-1 following 120 minutes of play. Aaron Loupalo-Bi had opened the scoring for Fleetwood in the 21st minute before Viktor Gyökeres equalised for Arsenal. The Premier League side was reduced to ten players in the 85th minute when 16-year-old Max Dowman received a red card. Belfast-born teenager Conor Haughey scored the decisive penalty to secure the quarter-final spot for the League Two club.

Coughlan's football journey began locally with Mungret Regional before he progressed to Limerick FC and subsequently moved to English side Huddersfield Town. After spells with Bray Wanderers, Cork City, Sligo Rovers, St Patrick’s Athletic—where he won the 2021 FAI Cup—and Waterford, he joined Fleetwood Town in 2024.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.localAngle: Limerick-born striker Ronan Coughlan helped secure Fleetwood Town's shock Carabao Cup victory over Arsenal, bringing national attention back to his footballing roots in Mungret Regional.
https://limerickvoice.com/?p=53250.originalTitle: Limerick striker stars in shock Carabao Cup upset over Arsenal

Photographs from the day captured the celebrations as the school community gathered to mark the occasion ahead of the mid-term break.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.headline: Limerick Libraries launch county-wide 'One Limerick, One Book' reading initiative
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.summary: Limerick Libraries and Creative Ireland have launched a new community reading initiative, selecting local author Karen Fitzgibbon's thriller 'Tell The Truth' as its inaugural title.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.story:
Bookworms across Limerick are being encouraged to read, discuss, and share the same novel under a newly launched county-wide reading initiative. 

'One Limerick, One Book' has been introduced by Limerick Libraries with support from the Creative Ireland Programme. Based on the successful 'One County, One Book' model, the scheme aims to connect communities throughout the city and county through a shared reading experience.

Thriller novel *Tell The Truth*, written by local author Karen Fitzgibbon, has been chosen as the very first title for the programme. Organisers based the selection on criteria including a strong local connection through the author, setting, or subject matter, broad appeal for general readers and book clubs, and sufficient availability of copies for a county-wide rollout.

Author Karen Fitzgibbon welcomed the announcement, describing her inclusion as a real honour. "A strong sense of place is incredibly important to me when I’m writing, and *Tell The Truth* is very much a Limerick story," she said.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.localAngle: The initiative connects readers across Limerick city and county through a shared reading experience featuring a local author and setting.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362612.originalTitle: New reading initiative launched in Limerick

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.headline: Rhebogue Mum Celebrates 18 Months Smoke-Free After QUIT Mid West Support
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.summary: Claire Crawford, 29, from Rhebogue has marked 18 months as a non-smoker after receiving support from QUIT Mid West during her fourth pregnancy at University Maternity Hospital Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.story:
A Limerick mother is celebrating nearly a year and a half free of cigarettes after getting support from the HSE’s QUIT Mid West service. 29-year-old Claire Crawford from Rhebogue had smoked since her teenage years and successfully kicked the habit after being referred through University Maternity Hospital Limerick (UMHL) during her fourth pregnancy.

Working with Stop Smoking Advisor Niamh Keating, Ms Crawford stopped smoking immediately upon referral and was completely nicotine-free within 20 weeks. She noted that previous attempts to quit during earlier pregnancies had failed because she could never last more than a few hours, but the regular advice and structure provided by the service made the crucial difference.

As well as health improvements, including better recovery after a caesarean section and the ability to breastfeed her youngest baby for the first time, Ms Crawford highlighted the financial impact. She previously spent around €150 a week on smoking, funds that are now redirected toward family activities and maintaining a smoke-free household for her children, coinciding with the national 'Stoptober' campaign.

Those looking for further information on quitting smoking can visit the HSE website at HSE.ie/QuitSmoking.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.localAngle: The story highlights a local mother from Rhebogue and her journey with the University Maternity Hospital Limerick-linked QUIT Mid West service.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362608.originalTitle: Limerick mum celebrates over one year smoke-free thanks to QUIT Mid West

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.headline: Council Warned Murdered Pensioner Over Illegal Tenant Living in Home
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.summary: The Central Criminal Court heard that Tipperary County Council flagged concerns to 89-year-old Josie Ray about an unauthorized occupant in her home months before she was allegedly murdered. The trial of Hasan Ali Gori, who has pleaded not guilty to the murder, is currently underway in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.story:
The Central Criminal Court heard this week that Tipperary County Council had contacted 89-year-old Josephine “Josie” Ray regarding concerns that a man was living illegally in her home prior to her alleged murder. Ms Ray, of St Joseph’s Park, Nenagh, was found strangled and smothered in her bed on August 4, 2024. The accused, 52-year-old Hasan Ali Gori, originally from Chad and with an address at St Joseph’s Park, has pleaded not guilty to the murder before Mr Justice Sean Gillane and a jury.

At the time of the alleged killing, Ali Gori was in a relationship with Ms Ray’s daughter, Mary Ray, who lived with an intellectual disability. Relatives and neighbours testified that the household was marked by constant arguments and fighting among the three residents. Seamus O’Brien, a community liaison officer with the council, gave evidence that he visited Ms Ray in April 2024 to inform her that, under her tenancy terms, no occupants other than her daughter were permitted in the property. A subsequent letter regarding anti-social behaviour and unauthorized occupancy was also sent to Ms Ray, warning that her tenancy was at risk.

Gardai told the court they responded to a domestic disturbance at the home on the night before Ms Ray was found dead. Garda Aoife Shine stated that Mary Ray was upset and claimed her partner was talking to prostitutes on his phone, while Ali Gori appeared frustrated. Another neighbour testified that he overheard the accused telling Mary Ray that either he had to go or Josie had to leave the house. The prosecution's case is that Ali Gori strangled and smothered the pensioner during the ongoing domestic friction.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.localAngle: The high-profile murder trial is taking place before the Central Criminal Court sitting in Limerick.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362605.originalTitle: Council told murder victim that accused was illegal tenant

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.headline: Limerick family-run Santa’s Magical Cabin marks 17 years and 700,000th customer
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.summary: The Limerick-operated festive attraction is celebrating its 17th year with six nationwide locations in partnership with Dunnes Stores, on track to welcome its 700,000th customer this Christmas.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.story:
Santa’s Magical Cabin is marking its 17th year of operation, with the Limerick family-run business on track to welcome its 700,000th customer across its six nationwide locations this Christmas. 

Operating in partnership with Dunnes Stores, the nationally recognised festive event employs 100 local people at its Limerick base during the Christmas season. The attraction features professional photography and has built a strong reputation for inclusivity, catering specifically to families with children who have additional needs, disabilities, and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD).

As part of its ongoing charity efforts, the company has partnered with the Jack & Jill Foundation for the third consecutive year, gifting 130 family visits across its six sites to Jack & Jill families. The attraction also offers corporate packages with bespoke booking codes for employee visits.

Santa will officially arrive at the Jetland Shopping Centre on Sunday, November 15, with pre-arrival entertainment including face painters, balloon artists, and festive characters beginning at 12:30pm ahead of his arrival at 1:30pm.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362593.localAngle: The nationally successful festive attraction is proudly Limerick family-owned and operated, employing 100 local staff each Christmas season at the Jetland Shopping Centre.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.summary: Limerick City and County Council is finalising a series of assessments regarding the Sheehy site in Abbeyfeale. The review includes examining a previous An Coimisiún Pleanála refusal and national retail planning guidelines.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.story:
Plans for the Sheehy site in Abbeyfeale have moved forward as Limerick City and County Council works to finalise a series of key assessments. Fine Gael councillor Liam Galvin was informed of the ongoing review following inquiries into the potential future of the West Limerick location.

According to Senior Council Planner Maria Woods, the local authority's current work involves reviewing the grounds behind a previous planning refusal from An Coimisiún Pleanála. Officials are also examining the relevant retail strategy context alongside the Department’s Retail Planning Guidelines as part of the process.

Ms Woods noted that any future proposal to rezone the Abbeyfeale property would require a substantial case to be made. “Should the Sheehy site be considered for rezoning, a robust planning argument and justification will be required to support any proposed change,” she stated.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.localAngle: The updates directly impact future development and planning strategy in the West Limerick town of Abbeyfeale.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362620.originalTitle: Update on plans for Sheehy site in Abbeyfeale

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362618.summary: More than 4,000 students from across the Mid West and beyond visited the Technological University of the Shannon in Limerick for the annual two-day open event.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362618.story:
More than 4,000 prospective students descended on the Technological University of the Shannon (TUS) Moylish campus for the university's annual two-day open event.

Held across Friday, October 15, and Saturday, October 16, the event welcomed visitors from the Mid West and further afield. Attendees were given the opportunity to explore the wide range of academic programmes available at the university and learn more about student life.

During the two-day event, prospective students had the chance to meet with current students and lecturers, as well as attend a packed schedule of course talks covering numerous disciplines. Visitors also engaged directly with representatives from Student Support, Access, Erasmus, and the Sports Office to gather information on campus resources and opportunities.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362618.localAngle: The event drew thousands of visitors to Limerick's TUS Moylish campus to explore higher education opportunities in the region.
