https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.headline: Former Milk Market takeaway transformed into training centre for adults with intellectual disabilities
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.summary: A disused takeaway unit at the Limerick Milk Market has been converted into a new training hub funded by The Michael Guinee Charitable Foundation. The Rising Together Training Centre will provide adults with intellectual disabilities pathways into employment through practical food and hospitality skills.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.story:
A disused takeaway unit at the heart of the Limerick Milk Market has been given a new lease of life as a fully equipped training facility for adults with intellectual disabilities. Funded by The Michael Guinee Charitable Foundation (MGCF), the new home of the Rising Together Training Centre (RTTC) aims to provide practical, vocational pathways into employment for its participants.

Open Monday to Friday, the centre offers training in baking, cooking, barista skills, catering, and hospitality. Alongside the educational programmes, the team will offer takeaway options including sandwiches, soups, treats, pizza slices, and pastries, as well as off-site catering services. 

David Fitzgerald, General Manager of the Limerick Milk Market, said the project delivers on a long-held ambition to establish a food training centre within Limerick's food community. Derek Barrett, Chief Executive of MGCF, noted that the project focuses on creating genuine opportunities for people with intellectual disabilities to participate more fully in employment and community life.

Laura Holland, Founder and CEO of Rising Together Training Programmes, highlighted the positive impact the initiative has had on participants' confidence and skill development. Meanwhile, Liam Flannery, Chairman of the Limerick Market Trustees, added that the centre will also benefit the wider local hospitality industry by supplying trained personnel ready to enter the workforce.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.localAngle: The initiative transforms a vacant unit inside the iconic Limerick Milk Market into an inclusive food training hub for the local community.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362633.originalTitle: Former takeaway unit at Limerick Milk Market given new lease of life

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362631.headline: Prison watchdog slams single nurse on duty for 755 inmates when Limerick gang figure died
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362631.summary: A damning report reveals just one nurse was on duty at Mountjoy Prison to handle medical emergencies for 755 inmates on the night Limerick native David Stanners died in his cell in 2023.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362631.story:
A prison watchdog has branded it "unacceptable" that only a single nurse was on duty to provide emergency medical responses for 755 prisoners on the night well-known Limerick gangland figure David Stanners died in his cell.

Mr Stanners, 51, originally from Pineview Gardens in Moyross, was serving a life sentence for the 2003 murder of rival gang member Kieran Keane. According to a new report from the Office of the Inspector of Prisons (OIP), prison staff entered his cell just before midnight on October 25, 2023, after an officer noticed they could not see him in his bed. The sole nurse on duty attempted CPR before an Advanced Paramedic later pronounced him dead at 00:30am. A postmortem later concluded he died from ischemic cardiomyopathy, alongside severe coronary artery disease and recent consumption of cocaine.

During a Critical Incident Review Meeting, the nurse who attempted resuscitation described how difficult it was for one staff member to perform prolonged CPR, a sentiment backed by the Chief Nurse Officer. Despite the OIP repeatedly recommending that prison officers be trained in CPR, the service continues to refuse. The watchdog noted that while the prison population has since surged to well over 1,000, a follow-up inspection in 2025 found that staffing levels at night remained unchanged at just one nurse.

In addition to the staffing concerns, the OIP recommended that doctors conduct clinical reviews when nursing staff raise alarms over the repeated requests and potential overuse of prescription medication by specific prisoners. The report highlighted that prior to his death, a nurse had noted Mr Stanners attended every drug round requesting paracetamol and required a GP review.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362574.headline: Singer-songwriter Shirley Callaghan releases dark folk single exploring Ireland's institutional legacy
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362574.summary: Limerick-connected singer-songwriter Shirley Callaghan has released 'House of Love', a dark folk track reflecting on the treatment of women and children in Ireland's institutions.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362574.story:
Singer-songwriter Shirley Callaghan has released her new single, 'House of Love', a dark folk track that examines the treatment of women and children within Ireland’s institutional system and the lasting legacy of those facilities after their closure.

Known for atmospheric songwriting and emotive vocals, Callaghan says the song looks beyond the walls of those institutions to focus on the psychological and emotional scars carried by survivors and their families. Though first asked to write the track years ago, the artist struggled to find an approach until a collaborative writing session in Málaga with fellow musicians Paul and Sandra.

“This is a song I was first asked to write a number of years ago. The subject stayed with me, and I made many attempts over the years to find a way into the song,” Callaghan said. “When Paul, Sandra and I eventually came together for a writing session in Málaga, the song finally found its voice.”

“House of Love comes from a very difficult part of recent Irish history, but for many people its consequences are not simply history,” she added. “I wanted the song to reflect something of that experience and to honour stories that needed to be told.” The single is currently available to stream and support on Bandcamp.

https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362622.headline: Limerick Councillors Clash with Mayor Moran Over Proposed Crescent Road Closure
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362622.summary: Elected representatives at the Metropolitan District meeting criticized Mayor John Moran’s plans to close The Crescent for six weeks over the Christmas period, arguing it disrupts traffic and impacts local businesses during peak trading.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362622.story:
Limerick councillors have voiced strong opposition to Mayor John Moran’s plans to close The Crescent during the busy Christmas shopping period. During the latest Metropolitan District meeting, local representatives questioned the necessity of the six-week road closure, arguing it disrupts traffic on a main artery into the city.

Elected members raised concerns that the closure would negatively impact traders and businesses in what they described as a core commercial district. Councillors suggested alternative locations for festive markets and events, such as Bedford Row, Thomas Street, or Cruises Street, to avoid causing disruption to shoppers and local businesses during peak retail weeks.

Cllr Joe Leddin called on Mayor Moran to reconsider the move and show leadership, noting that the area functions primarily as a business district rather than a retail hub. Cllr Catherine Slattery also criticized the decision to block off the road, stating she is standing up for local voices affected by the traffic restrictions, while other members questioned the ongoing rationale behind the recurring closures.
https://www.limerickpost.ie/?p=362622.localAngle: The proposed road closure directly affects traffic flow, retail trade, and shoppers navigating Limerick city centre during the Christmas period.
